preamble: A bilabial ejective [pʼ] is replaced by the bilabial implosive [ɓ]. Konso (Lowland East Cushitic) has no ejectives but has four implosives, ɓ ɗ ʄ ʛ. Orkaydo (2013: 8) describes a systematic correspondence in loans from Amharic: /pʼ/ becomes /ɓ/, just as /tʃʼ/ becomes /ʄ/ and /kʼ/ becomes /ʛ/, while /tʼ/ and /sʼ/ become plain t and s. A second, disputed case is inherited. Ehret (1987: 34, as cited in Wikipedia) reconstructs a rare Proto-Cushitic *pʼ, mainly on the basis of Dahalo pʼ and Yaaku ɓ, and takes Yaaku ɓ to continue it; most Cushitic languages show b in these words. Sasse (1979), as summarized in Wikipedia, separately derives Oromo pʼ from *b plus a laryngeal (see b → pʼ). The Yaaku examples come from a note in Wikipedia's summary of Ehret, which itself flags one cognate (Arbore ginɓa) as perhaps a borrowing from pre-Yaaku. The evidence is two loanwords in one language and two etymologies under a disputed reconstruction.
